content.text:
Your clone is on `main`, one commit ahead of `origin/main`, with uncommitted changes and untracked files. These commands preserve your commits and temporarily stash the unfinished work.

The URL you supplied appears malformed. Assuming the upstream is **`https://github.com/GitRollTraining/ai-full-stack-it-access-requests`**, run:

```bash
# Back up your current commits
git branch backup/main-before-upstream-merge

# Save uncommitted changes, including untracked files
git stash push --include-untracked -m "Work before upstream merge"

# Add and fetch the upstream repository
git remote add upstream https://github.com/GitRollTraining/ai-full-stack-it-access-requests.git
git fetch upstream

# Merge upstream changes into your main branch
git switch main
git merge upstream/main
```

If the merge reports conflicts, edit the conflicted files to preserve the intended changes, then run:

```bash
git add <resolved-file-paths>
git merge --continue
```

Alternatively, `git merge --abort` cancels the merge.

After the merge succeeds, restore your unfinished work:

```bash
git stash pop
```

If restoring the stash produces conflicts, resolve them; Git retains the stash when it cannot apply it cleanly.

Review and test the result, then update your fork:

```bash
git push origin main
```

This pushes your committed changes and the upstream merge. Your restored, uncommitted work remains local until you commit it.
